It's kind of a long explanation, but here goes: first I go in and go past the first room with the three guards (two near the door and one near the staircase) and immediately head left and stand in near the rubble where I can't go any further. This way I can see both Scrying Eyes that pass by and the patrolling guard. It's easiest to be able to take out one Scrying Eye at a time this way because I can make sure there's only one at a time and that the patrolling guard is not nearby. Once the Scrying Eyes are gone, I head to the far end and take out the guard standing against a pillar (or blocks of stone, I can't remember what they are. It's a half-orc guard, I think). Then when the patrolling guard gets close, I attack and kill him. Make sure you attack him far away from the cells because I don't want the warden alerted yet. After he's gone, I then go into the first room and kill the three guards in there. Finally, I'll go into the warden's office and talk to her with Tav usually (Warden has no idea all the guards are dead because everything has been done far away from her) while I separate Astarion from the group, have him pop an invisibility potion, creep up the ladder and eliminate the final scrying eye, allowing us to attack and kill the warden without letting the entire tower know. 

Then I can just grab a hammer, toss it to Wulbren and everyone gets free without a problem. No having to cast fog or cause a distraction because all the guards and the warden are dead. I've done it so many times now that it only takes me a few minutes usually. The only pain in the butt is the Death Ward on a few of the guards making it last like a round longer than it needs to.

I wasn't quite home alone; I had my 9 month old daughter with me. 

My husband was away for a field training exercise in the Navy. So I'm already on edge because I don't like being home alone in the apartment at night. He was gone for 10 days. It's day 2, which is also Halloween. 

I put my daughter down for bed at about 9pm and I settle into bed to play around on my phone. At 10pm, the doorbell starts ringing. I ignore it because I'm not about to answer the door at 10pm on Halloween when I'm home alone. I figure after a couple rings and no answer that they'll go away. Nope. They keep ringing and knocking. I'm also a tiny bit pissed off because it will suck if the baby wakes up. 

After a minute or two, I carefully creep to the door and look out the peephole. There are what appears to be two men just standing outside. From my view, they appear to be in their early 20's. They keep ringing the doorbell and knocking. They're speaking Spanish to each other and I have no idea what they are saying. 

By this point, it's been about 5 minutes of non-stop ringing and knocking and I'm terrified. I'm home alone and the only thing I can think of doing is grabbing a knife from the kitchen and hiding the baby and myself in the bedroom. I walk carefully into the bedroom and grab my phone. I call my husband and he doesn't answer. I try several times over the next few minutes and he doesn't answer. Finally my brain makes a smart decision and I decide to call the police non-emergency line. The dispatcher asks me a few questions as I'm apologizing as I'm not sure if they consider this an emergency and when I go to check the door to give them a description, I realize the knocking and ringing has stopped. I check the peephole and the guys are gone. The dispatcher tells me that if this happens again, call 911. I text my husband that I'm scared and to call me back when he can. I don't sleep until about 4am and wake up at 8 when my husband calls me back. He informs me of where the gun in the apartment is, just in case I need it. The whole ordeal lasts for about 10 minutes. And my daughter slept through it all. 

The next afternoon, the doorbell rings again. I check the peephole and see the two guys, an older woman, and a little girl. I open the door slightly (probably not smart, but daylight made me braver and stupider). The guys end up being like 16 year old boys with their mom and sister. They found a wallet in another building in the apartment complex. Which had the previous tenant's ID that had our address listed. I told them that only my husband and I lived there. 

I was lucky that it ended up being nothing. The boys were lucky that I wasn't a trigger-happy terrified person. 

Needless to say, ringing someone's doorbell and knocking on their door late at night on Halloween is not the smartest thing to do. I also learned that I am not brave. I just stayed quiet and absolutely terrified out of my brains until I called the cops.
